plan.topic: Months into tirzepatide and the scale is moving slower: what SURMOUNT-1's average curve shows about weight loss slowing over time
plan.angle: Title: 'Tirzepatide (Zepbound/Mounjaro): Scale Slowing Months In? #shorts'. Sentence 1: 'Tirzepatide and the scale slowing months in? In the big trial, average loss slowed too.' Then: averages aren't predictions, so look at the trend and other measures with your prescriber. Every number comes from L1's verified script. Everything else as briefed.
plan.working_title: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro): Scale Slowing Down Months In? #shorts
plan.why: Spin-off of L1. A felt progress moment that sends traffic into the after-6-months long video and the first-months series. | fact-check: The evidence is fine: in SURMOUNT-1 the average curve fell fastest early and flattened toward 72 weeks. Two risks. (1) The 'relief' framing could suggest that any one person's slowdown is normal or expected. Keep it to trial averages, and say plainly that only a prescriber can judge an individual's progress. (2) The brand in the title. SURMOUNT-1 tested adults with obesity or overweight without diabetes, which is Zepbound's approved use, not Mounjaro's. Every number must match L1's verified script exactly, so this Short can't be finalised until L1 passes its content check. Use no figure values that aren't marked 'about', and no week where the curve 'plateaus' unless the NEJM paper states it.

package.title: Tirzepatide (Zepbound): Average Loss Slowed Over 72 Weeks #shorts
package.description:
Tirzepatide, 72 weeks (SURMOUNT-1, adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes): average weight loss was fastest early, then flattened toward week 72. At week 72, the highest dose averaged 20.9% weight loss vs 3.1% on placebo. Averages are not predictions: 57% on the highest dose lost 20% or more of their body weight, vs 3% on placebo.
#tirzepatide
Not personal advice. Talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you.

script.cta:
Spoken: "The full video is on our channel." No subscribe line and no "link in the description".

Post notes:
- Watch-next target (Exp G): L1 "Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) After 6 Months: What to Expect?". Secondary: the First Month series playlist.
- Why the "full video" line stays: the 11-23 playbook scopes L1 as built on the label and SURMOUNT-1 to 72 weeks, so it covers this weight curve. The fact-checker's condition is met. If the publisher finds L1 does not cover the SURMOUNT-1 curve, cut "The full video is on our channel." and start s6 with "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber."
- Exact spoken word count: 152 if hyphenated words count as one, 157 if they count as two. There are 5 hyphenated words: seventy-two ×3, weight-related, fifty-seven. Both counts are inside the standard arm (135–160).
- To stay under 160 on either counting rule after adding "body" and the longer prescriber line, s5 was tightened.
- Fact-check fixes applied exactly:
  - s2 on-screen card
  - s3 on-screen card
  - s4 stat_label
  - s4 narration ("Even" removed, "body weight")
  - s5 closing line ("Your prescriber can help you make sense of it.")
- Title stays Zepbound, not Mounjaro, because SURMOUNT-1 tested adults without diabetes.
- Figures:
  - −20.9% vs −3.1% mean change at week 72
  - 57% vs 3% lost ≥20% of body weight, 15 mg vs placebo
  - Confirmed by the fact-checker against NEJM and ACC (src3 added).
  - No values are read off the figure and no plateau week is given.

factcheck.summary:
This Short passes. The science checks out, with a few minor on-screen fixes listed below.

**What I confirmed (SURMOUNT-1, NEJM 2022;387:205-216):**
- Mean weight change at week 72 was −20.9% on tirzepatide 15 mg vs −3.1% on placebo.
- 57% on 15 mg lost 20% or more of their body weight, vs 3% on placebo.
- Waist circumference and systolic blood pressure improved vs placebo.
- The population wording is right: adults with obesity, or overweight plus a weight-related condition, without diabetes.
- The 72-week curve does drop fastest early and then flattens.
- The hook pays off, framed as the trial average. No plateau week is invented, no dosing or medication-change advice is given, and the fixed safety line is copied exactly as one card.
- The Zepbound brand in the title fits a population without diabetes.

**What I couldn't check:**
- PubMed only returned a cookie page, so I confirmed the numbers through the American College of Cardiology's (ACC) trial summary and Lilly's results page.
- The post notes ask me to confirm the numbers match the L1 video's verified script. That script wasn't in this task, so I couldn't check it, and I didn't check that a matching full video exists.

**Minor fixes:**
1. Some on-screen cards are missing their measure, population or timeframe (s2, s4).
2. Check the post-notes word count: I count about 151 to 156 spoken words, not 155. Either way it's inside the 135–160 arm.
3. Two small softenings in the narration (s4's "Even", s5's "Only they").
4. Make sure the "full video" line points to a video that really covers this.

issues.problem: Fails the muted-viewer test. The card doesn't say what flattened (average weight), who was studied, or over what timeframe.
issues.fix: Avg weight in 72-wk trial: fastest drop early, then flattened

issues.problem: Missing the measure (body weight) and the timeframe (week 72), so a muted viewer could misread it.
issues.fix: Lost ≥20% of body weight at week 72: tirzepatide 15 mg vs placebo

issues.problem: The text card doesn't name the drug, the placebo group or the timeframe. The stat_label covers them only if it's shown on the same frame.
issues.fix: Tirzepatide 15 mg: −20.9% vs −3.1% placebo at 72 weeks

issues.claim: Even on the highest dose, fifty-seven percent lost twenty percent or more of their weight
issues.problem: "Even" makes 57% sound like a disappointment. It's the best responder rate in the trial. Also say "body weight", as the abstract does.
issues.fix: On the highest dose, fifty-seven percent lost twenty percent or more of their body weight, compared with three percent on placebo. More than half, but not everyone.

issues.claim: Only they can judge your progress.
issues.problem: Overstated: viewers can track their own progress too. The point is that the prescriber interprets the trend.
issues.fix: Your prescriber can help you make sense of it.

issues.claim: The full video is on our channel.
issues.problem: This promises a matching full video. The watch-next target is a Mounjaro 6-month video, and its population and figures couldn't be checked against this Short. Mounjaro is the type 2 diabetes brand, while SURMOUNT-1 tested adults without diabetes.
issues.fix: Keep the line only if the linked long video covers SURMOUNT-1's weight curve. Otherwise cut "The full video is on our channel." and start s6 with "Not personal advice, so ask your prescriber."

issues.problem: My count is about 151 if hyphenated words count as one and about 156 if they count as two. Both are within 135–160, but the logged count should be exact.
issues.fix: Recount and log the exact spoken word count, stating the counting rule (e.g. "151 words, hyphenated words counted as one").
